text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wendnesday:
- Swiss historian Peter Hug, who investigated Swiss-Polish correspondence with regard to unclaimed assets, said Switzerland transfered a total sum of 480,000 francs to Poland.
- All three big Basle-based pharmaceutical groups -- Ciba, Roche and Sandoz -- expect to raise net profits for fiscal 1996.
- Swiss Defence Minister Adolf Ogi launched a campaign calling for Switzerland to take part in Nato's Partnership for Peace. He said participation would not endanger Swiss neutrality.

- Swiss-Swedish group ABB reported a 24 percent rise in net profit to 809 million Swiss francs for the first nine months of this year. Chief executive Percy Barnevik said he expected a net profit to exceed last year's 1.315 billion francs.
- Swiss veterinarians said that they favoured a government plan to slaughter 230,000 cattle to eradicate the mad cow disease in Switzerland.

- Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger presented a 1997 federal budget which includes 44 billion Swiss francs of spending and a deficit of 5.5 billion Swiss francs. These figures are based on ecomonic growth of 1.5 percent.
